endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Data mix ratios: Document the ratio of domain-specific to general data in the fine-tuning set. Overreliance on domain-specific data can cause the model to lose general reasoning capabilities.

endorsements.title: AI-generated multiple-choice questions in health science education: Stakeholder perspectives and implementation considerations
endorsements.quote: Prompt engineering skills — the ability to effectively instruct AI systems to produce desired outputs — cannot be assumed and may necessitate the development of web portals that scaffold the question generation process.

endorsements.title: Ten tips for utilizing AI to generate high quality OSCE stations in medical education
endorsements.quote: To facilitate this, institutions can develop case templates that standardize structure across specialties ( 21 ).

evidence.title: Poetic or Prosaic? Evaluating the Linguistic Quality of AI-Generated Draft Replies to Patient Portal Messages
evidence.outcome: Token retention of AI drafts across prompt refinement phases
evidence.effect: Prompt refinements (Phases 2–4 vs Phase 1) increased token retention of drafts in final physician messages.
evidence.quote: Prompt refinements increased token retention.

evidence.title: The effects of ChatGPT on patient education of knee osteoarthritis: a preliminary study of 60 cases
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT answer quality and patient knowledge: structured question outline vs free use
evidence.effect: Answer quality 92.1 ± 4.3 (outline) vs 81.4 ± 10.4 (free), P = 0.001; knowledge 95.3 ± 4.7 (outline) vs 82.1 ± 12.3 (free) vs 95.6 ± 5.3 (physician).
evidence.quote: With the outline given to patients, ChatGPT gave higher-quality answers compared with the answers from the group with free education (92.1 ± 4.3 versus 81.4 ± 10.4, P = 0.001).

evidence.title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Physician acceptance of AI-drafted replies after iterative, versioned prompt engineering
evidence.effect: Acceptance of draft suitability rose from 62% to 84% (P<.001) in the validation set (N=200); 74% of production drafts were rated helpful.
evidence.quote: After 3 iterations of prompt engineering, physician acceptance of draft suitability increased from 62% to 84% (P <.001) in the validation dataset (N = 200), and 74% of drafts in the test dataset were rated as "helpful."

evidence.title: Prompt engineering with a large language model to assist providers in responding to patient inquiries: a real-time implementation in the electronic health record
evidence.outcome: Provider use of and negative sentiment toward GPT-4 drafts, engineered vs original prompt
evidence.effect: Negative sentiment fell from 12.0% to 8.2% (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.36-0.52), but message usage decreased in the mixed model (beta -0.10, 95% CI -0.11 to -0.09, P<.01).
evidence.quote: In mixed linear regression accounting for the provider and number of messages per provider, the engineered prompt in the post-period was associated with a decrease in message usage (beta coefficient, −0.10; 95% CI, −0.11 to −0.09, P < .01).

evidence.title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated dialogue quality across iteratively refined prompt versions V1-V3
evidence.effect: Significant differences across all 6 dimensions (all P<.001); medians increased progressively from V1 to V3 with reduced dispersion.
evidence.quote: Overall differences among prompt versions were statistically significant across all 6 dimensions (Kruskal-Wallis test, all P values <.001).

evidence.title: Prompt engineering does not universally improve Large Language Model performance across clinical decision-making tasks
evidence.outcome: clinical decision-making performance across sequential tasks
evidence.effect: Prompt engineering significantly improved performance on relevant diagnostic testing but was counterproductive for other tasks.
evidence.quote: While it significantly improved the performance on the task with lowest baseline accuracy (relevant diagnostic testing), it was counterproductive for others.

evidence.title: Prompting is All You Need: How to Make LLMs More Helpful for Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Guideline adherence, unsafe recommendations, and grading accuracy with structured (CARDS) vs simple prompts
evidence.effect: For GPT-4o and o3, structured prompts raised guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, cut unsafe recommendations from 16.7% to 0%, and raised grading accuracy from 0% to 100%. Llama models gained less.
evidence.quote: For some closed-source models (GPT-4o, o3), prompts structured in the CARDS style improved guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, eliminated unsafe recommendations (16.7% to 0%), and increased specific guideline grading accuracy from 0% to 100%.

evidence.title: Harnessing Large Language Models for Reliable Automatic Charlson Comorbidity Index Scoring: A Validation Study
evidence.outcome: effect of structured prompting on consistency
evidence.effect: Structured prompting further improved consistency; no numeric effect reported.
evidence.quote: Open-source and proprietary systems achieved comparable accuracy, and structured prompting further improved consistency.

evidence.title: Exploration of ChatGPT application in diabetes education: a multi-dataset, multi-reviewer study
evidence.outcome: Helpfulness and trustworthiness ratings of ChatGPT responses with crafted prompts versus physicians
evidence.effect: Ratings of ChatGPT responses with carefully crafted prompts were comparable to physicians, whereas uncrafted responses were rated lower (helpfulness: 4.18 vs. 4.91, P <0.001; trustworthiness: 4.80 vs. 5.20, P = 0.042).
evidence.quote: However, when carefully crafted prompts were utilized, the ratings of ChatGPT responses were comparable to those of physicians.

evidence.title: Enhancing Public Healthcare with IoT and AI: A Comprehensive Study on Improving Dry Eye Disease Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: AI response accuracy with specialized prompting
evidence.effect: Prompted versus non-prompted queries increased accuracy from 80.1–99.6%.
evidence.quote: A comparison between prompted and non-prompted queries reveals a significant accuracy increase from 80.1–99.6%.

evidence.title: Automated HEART score determination via ChatGPT: Honing a framework for iterative prompt development
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
evidence.outcome: Effect of iterative prompt refinement on LLM output validity and accuracy
evidence.effect: Across three iterations, GPT-4 mean error decreased from 0.16 to 0.10 and non-numerical responses fell for both models; GPT-3.5 mean error stayed at 0.42.
evidence.quote: For GPT‐4, this same average error decreased from 0.16 (0.11–0.22) to 0.10 (0.07–0.14) points.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic clinical notes (four simulated patients; 1200 queries per model)

evidence.title: Use of a large language model with instruction-tuning for reliable clinical frailty scoring
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
evidence.outcome: consistency and inter-rater reliability of Clinical Frailty Scale scoring
evidence.effect: Instruction-tuned prompt achieved Fleiss' Kappa of 0.887 with consistent responses in all scenarios; score distributions differed significantly from basic prompt in 5 of 7 scenarios.
evidence.quote: The instruction-tuned prompt showed high inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' Kappa of 0.887) and produced consistent responses in all scenarios.

evidence.title: Evaluating cognitive performance: Traditional methods vs. ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: GPT-3.5 scoring discrepancies after refined prompts and scoring rules
evidence.effect: Refined interaction protocols and scoring rules reduced most GPT-3.5 vs physician differences; only memory sections 8 and 14 remained different (P<0.05).
evidence.quote: After testing, optimizing the interaction process and scoring rules can reduce most of the differences, with only differences observed in 8th and 14th sections of memory ( P < 0.05), and no significant differences observed in the rest ( P > 0.05) ( Figure 6 ).

evidence.title: [EMERGING THERAPIES FOR LI-FRAUMENI SYNDROME AND RHABDOMYOSARCOMA: CAN CHAT GPT ASSESS THE THERAPIES IT SUGGESTS USING THE BRADFORD-HILL CRITERIA?]
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and clinical usefulness by prompt structure
evidence.effect: Targeted prompts generated more accurate and clinically useful responses; no numerical results reported.
evidence.quote: Targeted prompts (instructions for structuring the response, formulated as questions) lead to the generation of more accurate and clinically useful model responses but these, too, should be approached with caution.

evidence.title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
evidence.outcome: structured prompt changes reduced note errors
evidence.effect: Major hallucinations reduced 75% (4 to 1), major omissions 58% (24 to 10), and minor omissions 35% (114 to 74).
evidence.quote: The change in the prompt from Experiments 3 to 8 reduced the incidence of major hallucinations by 75% (from 4 to 1), major omissions by 58% (24 to 10), and minor omissions by 35% (114 to 74) (Fig. 8 ).

evidence.title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
evidence.outcome: MEWS triage accuracy before vs after prompt engineering with structured prompt
evidence.effect: GPT-4-Turbo accuracy rose from 63.93% to 100%; GPT-4o from 63.41% to 96.20%; average difference from standard score fell to 0 and 0.08.
evidence.quote: GPT-4-Turbo achieved an impressive accuracy of 100% across all the 10 runs.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

evidence.title: Enhancing responses from large language models with role-playing prompts: a comparative study on answering frequently asked questions about total knee arthroplasty
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, comprehensiveness, acceptability with role-playing prompt template vs zero-shot prompting
evidence.effect: GPT-3.5 acceptability rose from 45% to 72.5% and GPT-4 from 55% to 77.5% with role-play; GPT-3.5 accuracy 3.33 to 3.70. Effects not significant for Gemini or Claude.
evidence.quote: Role-playing prompts also significantly enhanced the acceptability rate of ChatGPT-4 ( P = 0.033).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (10 questions x 4 models x 2 prompt types)

evidence.title: Prompting Pro Tips! Best Practices for Generating Clinical Narrative Summaries
evidence.outcome: clinical adequacy, hallucinations, and bias
evidence.effect: Structured adequacy 39% compared to 9%, but structured prompts were more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.
evidence.quote: The structured approach was more likely to produce a clinically adequate summary (39% compared to 9%) but also more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.
evidence.sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on 8 clinical scenarios each with structured and vague prompts

evidence.title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
evidence.outcome: detailed prompting and guideline adherence
evidence.effect: Detailed prompts improved vital signs from 33 to 91%, second-line dosages from 50 to 100%, third-line dosages from 0 to 100%, complications from 0 to 100%.
evidence.quote: More specific and detailed prompts increased guideline adherence most markedly regarding vital sign assessment (from 33 to 91%), correct dosages of second-line (from 50 to 100%), third-line drugs (from 0 to 100%), and screening for complications (from 0 to 100%).

evidence.title: Enhancing the CAD-RADS™ 2.0 Category Assignment Performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Through "Few-shot" Prompting
evidence.outcome: CAD-RADS category assignment accuracy with structured few-shot prompt versus zero-shot prompt
evidence.effect: Zero-shot accuracy 14% (ChatGPT) and 8% (DeepSeek); few-shot improved to 98% and 93% (both P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Few-shot prompting significantly improved accuracy to 98% for ChatGPT and 93% for DeepSeek (both P <0.001) and eliminated hallucinations.

evidence.title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Total clinical performance score by prompt strategy (meta-cognitive vs zero-shot)
evidence.effect: Meta-cognitive prompts scored 73.2 vs 64.8 for zero-shot (p<0.001, d=0.62); safety-first 72.1; residual safety and bias concerns persisted.
evidence.quote: This approach demonstrated significant advantages over zero-shot reasoning (64.8 ± 15.3 points, 95% CI: 58.2–71.4, 58.9%; p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.62) and structured reasoning (67.9 ± 13.7 points, 61.7%; p = 0.02, Cohen’s d = 0.42), with effect sizes indicating moderate to large practical significance.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
evidence.outcome: Output quality after structured prompting
evidence.effect: Composite score improved overall (p = 0.019); evidence quality improved +0.765, +1.106, and +0.425 with p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: The analysis of the structured prompt’s effect revealed that this approach led to a small but statistically significant improvement in the composite score across all LLMs.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical infection control scenarios (165 outputs rated by 16 experts)

evidence.title: A deterministic large language model (LLM) framework for safe, protocol-adherent clinical decision support: application in hemodialysis anemia management (AnemiaCare HDs)
evidence.outcome: protocol adherence of clinical recommendations
evidence.effect: protocol adherence increased from 32% (96/300) with loosely structured prompting to 100% (300/300) with deterministic prompt templates (p < 0.001)
evidence.quote: The improvement from Phase 1 to Phase 2 was highly significant (32% vs. 100%, p < 0.001, Fisher’s exact test).

evidence.title: Prompt-Driven ChatGPT Carbon Calculator for Dental Practices: Estimation and Tailored Improvement Strategies
evidence.outcome: accuracy and specificity
evidence.effect: Variant 1 produced no specific footprint; Variant 2 provided 12 recommendations; Variant 3 provided 17; Chat waste estimate 232.2 kg versus Excel 246.1 kg.
evidence.quote: Structured prompts improved both accuracy and specificity.
evidence.sample_unit: prompt variants tested with one mock dental practice dataset

evidence.title: Leveraging ChatGPT for thematic analysis of medical best practice advisory data
evidence.outcome: structured prompting effect on agreement
evidence.effect: Role + context raised Category 2 agreement to 73% (κ = 0.73); all strategies reached 83% (κ = 0.76) in Category 1.
evidence.quote: Here, prompt refinements made a much larger difference: role + context (I1) yielded the greatest improvement, raising agreement to 73% (κ = 0.73, substantial).

evidence.title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
evidence.venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
evidence.outcome: HAS-BLED scoring accuracy before vs after prompt optimization with guideline criteria
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 accuracy rose from 24% to 89%, ChatGPT-4o Deep Research from 51% to 95% (P < .001).
evidence.quote: Specifically, the accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 increased from 24% to 89%, while that of ChatGPT-4o Deep Research improved from 51% to 95%.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

evidence.title: AI-Generated Exercise Prescriptions for At-Risk Populations: Safety and Feasibility of a Large Language Model Assessed by Expert Evaluation
evidence.outcome: safety and guideline alignment across prompt structuring stages
evidence.effect: Safety increased from 3.69 to 4.07 and Guideline Alignment from 3.80 to 4.16 from Stage 1 to 2, but plateaued or declined at Stage 3 (3.69 and 3.98)
evidence.quote: Prompt structuring from Stage 1 to Stage 2 was associated with improved mean scores in safety and guideline alignment.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated exercise prescriptions (3 cases x 3 prompt stages x 5 repetitions) rated by 3 experts

evidence.title: Multidimensional evaluation of large language models in radiology report readability
evidence.outcome: Key information point accuracy with unoptimized vs optimized structured prompts
evidence.effect: Accurate KIP: ChatGPT-4.0 52.2% to 86.1%; DeepSeek-R1 61.7% to 91.1%; Grok-3 99.4% to 100%
evidence.quote: Using the optimized prompt framework, quantitative results showed that the optimized prompts significantly improved the translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 and Deep Seek-R1, as evidenced by higher key information point (KIP) retention rates (Table 5 ).
evidence.sample_unit: radiology reports (plus 800 patients in clinical setting validation)

evidence.title: Hidden failure modes of large language models in healthcare-associated infection surveillance: a structured evaluation using NHSN definitions
evidence.outcome: accuracy by prompt structure
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved from 78.6% standard to 88.6% structured and 95.7% constrained; Cochran’s Q(2) = 18.2, P < .001.
evidence.quote: The constrained (95.7%) and structured (88.6%) prompts showed higher accuracy than the standard (78.6%) prompt (McNemar P = .00049 and P = .0156, respectively).
evidence.sample_unit: case-prompt classifications (70 synthetic vignettes x 3 prompting strategies)

evidence.title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
evidence.outcome: initial hypertension treatment decision accuracy
evidence.effect: Guidance-based prompt strategies improved ChatGPT-4.1 accuracy from 64.0% (zero-shot) to 91.3% (Guidance-Self-Consistency), Claude-4 from 65.0% to 88.3%, Gemini-2.5 Pro from 64.33% to 87.7%, and DeepSeek-V3 from 62.7% to 86.3%.
evidence.quote: Guidance-based prompt engineering strategies significantly enhanced model accuracy on Task 1 compared to zero-shot prompting.

evidence.title: Evaluating open-source LLMs for dental EMR generation
evidence.outcome: AI-generated dental EMR quality
evidence.effect: CRISPE improved total 7DI: 28.86 ± 2.12 vs. 26.91 ± 2.36; p < .001; d = 0.57.
evidence.quote: As detailed in Table 3 , the CRISPE framework yielded a highly significant improvement in overall 7DI scores (28.86 ± 2.12 vs. 26.91 ± 2.36; p < .001, Cohen’s d = 0.57).
evidence.sample_unit: de-identified dental EMRs converted to synthetic Mandarin dialogues (50-case expert-rated subset)

evidence.title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
evidence.outcome: communication quality total score
evidence.effect: Mean score was 17.95 ± 1.62 for configured model vs 9.55 ± 1.94 for baseline (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.22); 97.5% vs 0% met high quality criteria
evidence.quote: CSA-GPT achieved higher total rubric scores than ChatGPT5.2 (17.95 ± 1.62; 95% CI: 17.59–18.31 vs. 9.55 ± 1.94; 95% CI: 9.12–9.98; p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.22), noting that the rubric is a theory-informed, exploratory benchmarking instrument.

evidence.title: Shaping AI in Pelvic Floor Physiotherapy: The Impact of Role-Play Prompting on ChatGPT Response Quality
evidence.outcome: Rater-scored response quality (relevance, accuracy, comprehensiveness, clarity) under role-play vs neutral prompt
evidence.effect: Persona-based prompting significantly improved quality across all domains (p < 0.001); mean differences: comprehensiveness 1.45, relevance 1.12, accuracy 0.88, clarity 1.48; Cohen's d 1.66-2.11.
evidence.quote: Persona-based prompting significantly improved response quality across all domains (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Safety-oriented prompt correction
evidence.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 improved all five dimensions (p<0.001), largest in Safety B=0.91 (3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness B=0.86 (2.91 to 3.76).
evidence.quote: Linear mixed model estimates of marginal means ( Figure 5 and Table 4 ) showed that the corrected prompt significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 across all five dimensions ( p < 0.001), with the largest gains in Safety ( B = 0.91, from 3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness ( B = 0.86, from 2.91 to 3.76).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

evidence.title: Comparison of Large Language Model-Based Systems and Prompt Engineering for Internal Medicine Clinical Pharmacy Cases
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompt engineering template on accuracy and completeness of LLM responses
evidence.effect: No statistically significant interaction between LLM system and prompt template for accuracy and completeness; template did not improve accuracy and completeness.
evidence.quote: Logistic regression modeling demonstrated no statistically significant interactions between the two LLM-based systems and use of a prompt engineering template for accuracy and completeness.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Caries Risk Assessment: Evaluating the Current Status of Caries Management by Risk Assessment and Cariogram with Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Effect of structured guideline-based prompts versus unguided prompts on LLM output accuracy
evidence.effect: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with unguided prompting (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with the unguided condition (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Automated risk scoring for venous thromboembolism using large language models with expert knowledge-augmented prompting: a multicenter validation study
evidence.outcome: VTE risk scoring agreement and F1 score
evidence.effect: Expert knowledge-augmented prompts had highest performance; test mean item-level PABAK and F1 were 0.97 and 0.96 for Padua, and 0.97 and 0.93 for Caprini.
evidence.quote: Expert knowledge-augmented prompts showed the highest performance in both datasets.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
evidence.outcome: Quality and consistency of LLM outputs with optimized structured prompt (PROMPORT) versus zero-shot
evidence.effect: PROMPORT stabilized mDISCERN and JAMA profiles over time and reduced linguistic variance versus unprompted models, which showed significant temporal volatility (p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: In conclusion, while unprompted models exhibit marked baseline linguistic and quality variations, the strategic integration of robust prompt engineering successfully enforces the temporal stability and clarity required for reliable digital public health communication.

evidence.title: The use of structured prompt to improve the readability, accuracy, and quality of ChatGPT responses on labor epidural analgesia: a brief report
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT responses using structured prompt template versus direct questions
evidence.effect: Accuracy 99.8% ± 0.2% with CRAFT prompt vs 99.0% ± 0.4% with direct questions, P = 0.029; no difference in understandability or actionability.
evidence.quote: Accuracy was significantly higher in CRAFT-based prompt group than direct-question group (99.8% ± 0.2% vs. 99.0% ± 0.4%, P = 0.029).

evidence.title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
evidence.outcome: Model output variance and accuracy under baseline versus optimized structured prompts
evidence.effect: Optimized structured prompts significantly reduced output variance and improved translational accuracy, especially in DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4.0.
evidence.quote: Optimized structured prompting can substantially reduce the variability of model outputs and improve the accuracy of medical text translation.

evidence.title: AI Simplification of Dermatopathology Reports for Patients: Basic Versus Prompt-Engineered Approaches
evidence.outcome: report factualness, completeness, and potential harm
evidence.effect: Prompt engineering showed no advantage; DermDecoder had worse completeness in psoriasis (p=0.007) and harmfulness in molluscum contagiosum (p=0.049) and melanoma in situ (p=0.048)
evidence.quote: Prompt engineering offered no advantage over basic AI usage in balancing professional accuracy with patient accessibility, necessitating human-in-the-loop oversight for AI-generated explanations.
evidence.sample_unit: dermatology and dermatopathology professionals rating six fictitious reports

evidence.title: Evaluation of Prompt Design and Internal Reasoning in Chatbot-Based Medical History Taking: Simulation Study
evidence.outcome: Checklist history coverage
evidence.effect: Prompt detail was significant: F1,65=56.74; P<.001; η²G=0.085; DT mean coverage 72.3% vs MN 54.0%.
evidence.quote: This analysis showed significant main effects of prompt detail ( F 1, 65 =56.74; P <.001; η² G =0.085) and internal reasoning ( F 1, 65 =47.45; P <.001; η² G =0.096).

evidence.title: Prompting generative artificial intelligence to create plain language patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of outputs from advanced structured prompt vs basic prompt
evidence.effect: Advanced plain-language prompt produced PEMs that were readable, understandable, and actionable, with comparable results across ChatGPT and Gemini.
evidence.quote: A plain-language prompt for generative AI created PEMs that were readable, understandable, and actionable, with comparable results across two AI programs.

evidence.title: Evaluating a Guideline-Integrated Clinical Interaction Framework Vs a Standard Large Language Model Interaction for Dietary Recommendations in Recurrent Urolithiasis: In Silico Study
evidence.outcome: metabolic specificity, guideline adherence, and actionability
evidence.effect: StoneAgent scored higher than standard LLM across metabolic specificity (median 5.00 vs 3.00), guideline adherence (5.00 vs 3.67), and actionability (5.00 vs 3.00; all P<.001).
evidence.quote: In the structured-input experiment, StoneAgent achieved higher performance than the standard LLM across metabolic specificity, guideline adherence, and actionability, with median case-level scores of 5.00 (IQR 5.00-5.00) vs 3.00 (IQR 2.75-3.92) for metabolic specificity, 5.00 (IQR 5.00-5.00) vs 3.67 (IQR 3.08-4.00) for guideline adherence, and 5.00 (IQR 5.00-5.00) vs 3.00 (IQR 2.67-3.33) for actionability (all P<.001).

evidence.title: Hierarchical Reasoning Gates for Multimodal Large Language Models in Dental Image Interpretation: A Prompt-Level Protocol for Improving Accuracy
evidence.outcome: Image-interpretation accuracy of structured versus zero-shot prompt architectures
evidence.effect: Mean Total Score rose from 3.47 ± 1.33 (zero-shot P1) to 4.77 ± 0.68 (HRG P3); Full Accuracy rose from 23.3% to 86.7%; failures on 3 or more variables fell from 20.0% to 3.3%.
evidence.quote: Mean Total Score increased from 3.47 ± 1.33 for P1 to 4.77 ± 0.68 for P3, while Full Accuracy increased from 23.3% to 86.7%.

evidence.title: De novo generation of colorectal patient educational materials using large language models: Prompt engineering key to improved readability
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM output by prompt type (Basic, Iterative, Metric-based)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT Metric-based prompt improved readability vs baseline: Grade Level 5.2 vs 8.1, Modified Grade Level 7.3 vs 10.3, Ease 70.5 vs 60.4, all P<.01; other prompts and Perplexity varied.
evidence.quote: The variability in performance highlights the importance of the prompt used with large language models.
evidence.sample_unit: colorectal surgery patient educational topics (baseline materials and matched LLM-generated documents)

evidence.title: Developing artificial intelligence tools for institutional review board pre-review: A pilot study on ChatGPT's accuracy and reproducibility
evidence.outcome: custom versus standard prompt variability
evidence.effect: GPTs-3 extracted 2.0 benefits (SD 0.0; min/max 2/2); standard prompts 5.3 (SD 1.8; min 3, max 8).
evidence.quote: In contrast, outputs generated using standard prompts showed greater variability in both the number and type of extracted participant-related benefits, with categories and counts differing significantly across trials ( Tables 4 and 5 ).
evidence.sample_unit: trials (10 per custom GPT per model, plus 10 standard-prompt trials)

evidence.title: Exploring GPT-4o's multimodal reasoning capabilities with panoramic radiograph: the role of prompt engineering
evidence.outcome: radiograph error identification
evidence.effect: Meta prompt vs zero-shot improved recall 43.33% to 52.67%, accuracy 39.95% to 68.75%, and F1 0.42 to 0.60.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o with the meta prompt demonstrated improvements in recall (43.33% vs. 52.67%, P = 0.022), accuracy (39.95% vs. 68.75%, P < 0.001), and F1 score (0.42 vs. 0.60, P < 0.001) compared to the zero-shot prompt and other prompt strategies.

evidence.title: A Multimodal Large Language Model as an End-to-End Classifier of Thyroid Nodule Malignancy Risk: Usability Study
evidence.outcome: prompt engineering accuracy and consistency
evidence.effect: Composition accuracy improved 56.3% vs 41.9%, but shape, margins, and overall TI-RADS worsened; overall consistency improved 59.5% vs 36%.
evidence.quote: However, prompt engineering had a mixed effect on accuracy.

evidence.title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
evidence.outcome: T-staging accuracy with explicit prompts
evidence.effect: With explicit instructions, all models achieved > 90% T-staging accuracy; Chinese T all-model average was 92.8% with prompt versus 79.7% without.
evidence.quote: In our study, all models demonstrated high performance levels under ideal conditions with explicit instructions, achieving > 90% accuracy in T-staging tasks and indicating strong baseline capabilities.
evidence.sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

evidence.title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
evidence.outcome: Prompt/session protocol concordance
evidence.effect: Systematic RPE plus ZSR elevated CAP concordance from 70-80% baseline to over 95%.
evidence.quote: The key insight is that diagnostic accuracy is driven not by model size or architecture, but by systematic RPE and the ZSR protocol, the latter proving essential for eliminating conversational bias and elevating concordance with CAP consensus from a baseline of 70-80% to over 95%.

evidence.title: Safety-Oriented Benchmarking of Large Language Models in Risk-Based Management of Abnormal Cervical Screening Results: Scenario-Based Benchmark Study
evidence.outcome: Effect of guideline-directed prompt package versus baseline prompt on safety and concordance
evidence.effect: Guideline-directed prompt package associated with higher odds of unsafe major error-free performance (OR 3.76, 95% CI 2.45-5.77) and exact concordance (OR 8.27, 95% CI 4.14-16.52).
evidence.quote: In the main-effects model, the guideline-directed prompt package was associated with higher odds of both unsafe major error-free performance (odds ratio [OR] 3.76, 95% CI 2.45-5.77; P<.001) and exact concordance (OR 8.27, 95% CI 4.14-16.52; P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: model responses (60 synthetic scenarios x 3 models x 2 prompt arms x 3 repetitions)

evidence.title: Reliability of Large Language Model Generated Clinical Reasoning in Assisted Reproductive Technology: Blinded Comparative Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: prompt strategy effect on CoT quality
evidence.effect: Random Few-shot offered no significant improvement over Zero-shot; Selective Few-shot outperformed all human metrics (p < .001).
evidence.quote: Critically, the Random Few-shot strategy offered no significant improvement over the Zero-shot baseline, demonstrating that low-quality examples are as ineffective as no examples.

commentary.bottom_line: Structured or refined prompts improved accuracy, guideline adherence, or clinician acceptance in most of the 52 tests, and one deployment study tracked iterative, versioned prompt changes, but no study tested governance review of templates. Several studies found that structured prompts added hallucinations, lowered accuracy on some tasks, or helped some models and not others, so templates may need validation for each task and model.

perspectives.view: One randomized trial (n=60) and three real-deployment before-after or quasi-experimental studies support refined prompts, and a fourth deployment study had mixed results. Most other tests are simulations comparing structured with simple prompts, which is indirect to governance-reviewed templates. The endorsing framework quote addresses fine-tuning data ratios, and the other two endorsements are education commentaries.

Structured prompts cut major hallucinations in notes from 4 to 1 and major omissions from 24 to 10. In stroke vignettes, unsafe recommendations fell from 16.7% to 0%. One study found that structured prompts introduced more hallucinations and bias, and another found prompt engineering counterproductive for some tasks. Templates may therefore need safety review for each task.

After iterative, versioned prompt changes, physician acceptance of drafted replies rose from 62% to 84%. Draft token retention also increased across refinement phases. A second deployment found that negative sentiment fell from 12.0% to 8.2% while draft usage decreased (beta -0.10). Better-rated drafts may not translate into more use.

A language-simplification prompt lowered accuracy for Kimi from 70.0% to 48.8% and for DouBao from 57.5% to 7.5%. In texts for older and low-literacy readers, DISCERN scores differed by prompt for all 6 models. Plain-language templates may trade accuracy for readability. Positive tests in China involved general and stroke patients, not US safety-net groups.

No study reported the staff time or cost of building, reviewing, or maintaining a template library. Template gains varied by model. Role-play templates helped GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 but not Gemini or Claude, and GPT-3.5 error stayed at 0.42 after refinement. A template may need revalidation whenever the underlying model changes.

In the one randomized trial, patients who used a structured question outline reached knowledge scores of 95.3, close to 95.6 with a physician and above 82.1 with free use. In a hazard study, framing a prompt as coming from a patient produced under-triage in 41.7% of responses, compared with 12.5% for specialist framing.

commentary.research_gap: No study compared a governance-reviewed, versioned template library with ad hoc prompting on patient outcomes, error rates reaching patients, or clinician workload in routine care. No study measured how template performance changes after model updates, or the cost of maintaining templates across sites.
commentary.underserved_note: Six tests of the practice were conducted in China or Germany, four of which were tagged as using non-English data, and one included older stroke survivors. No test of the practice included Medicaid, safety-net, US limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Hazard studies suggest that simplification prompts can reduce accuracy, so templates aimed at these groups would need separate validation.
